Arrive AI and Modovolo plan automated drone-to-station deliveries

The partners will integrate Lift drones with Arrive Point stations, progressing through development and testing before proposed food deliveries.

Arrive AI / Newswire ↗9 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2

Automating the final handoff

Arrive AI announced a partnership with Modovolo on October 9 to develop delivery into secure, climate-assisted Arrive Point stations. The aim is to eliminate a person waiting at the destination or a parcel left on a doorstep. This is a joint development programme, rather than an announcement of an already operating delivery network.

Aircraft, station and software

Modovolo’s Lift platform combines modular payload provisions with RTK localization. Arrive Point and Arrive OS support the goods exchange. Modovolo says work starts with a winch prototype to lower parcels into the station. Precise handoff and coordination between aircraft and ground infrastructure are central integration tasks.

Testing precedes customer service

Integration and headquarters testing will support staff training and operational simulation. Successful tests and required approvals would precede proposed food deliveries in a designated Fishers, Indiana area. The announcement gives no launch date, fleet count or integrated-system payload, so it should not be read as generally available customer service.
